Very active area: the remaining window may be closed soon
Historically associated with Segre, but the problem's standard name is not a person's
plain: An arc in F_q^k is a set of vectors in which every k of them are linearly independent. Arcs are the same thing as linear MDS codes, the codes that meet the Singleton bound, and Reed-Solomon codes give arcs of size q+1. Show that q+1 is always the maximum when q is odd and 2 ≤ k ≤ q. This is known when q is prime (Ball 2012). A 2026 preprint claims it for all k outside a middle window of roughly q/(2p−3) dimensions, where p is the characteristic; the smallest open case would then be q=27 with 12 ≤ k ≤ 17.
math: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and $2\le k\le q$. Prove that if $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^k$ is a set of vectors such that every $k$ distinct elements of $S$ are linearly independent, then $|S|\le q+1$.

q (odd q is the same as odd characteristic; every odd prime power is realized). Vectors in F_q^k
are `Fin k → F`; S is a `Finset`. "Every k distinct elements are linearly independent" is: for
every sub-finset T ⊆ S with |T| = k, the family of elements of T (indexed by the subtype of T)
is `LinearIndependent F`. This is the standard notion of an arc (equivalently, the columns of a
generator matrix of a linear [|S|, k] MDS code; duplicate columns cannot occur since S is a set,
and a repeated vector would make some k-subset dependent anyway). Claim: every such arc has at
most q+1 elements whenever 2 ≤ k ≤ q. ¬Claim means an arc of size q+2 in some F_q^k with q odd
and 2 ≤ k ≤ q.

namespace OpenProblems.QEDM136
noncomputable section

/-- `S ⊆ F^k` is an arc: every `k` distinct elements are linearly independent. -/
def IsArc {F : Type} [Field F] (k : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin k → F)) : Prop :=
  ∀ T : Finset (Fin k → F), T ⊆ S → T.card = k →
    LinearIndependent F (fun v : {x // x ∈ T} => (v.1 : Fin k → F))

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [Fintype F], Odd (Fintype.card F) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k ≤ Fintype.card F →
      ∀ S : Finset (Fin k → F), IsArc k S → S.card ≤ Fintype.card F + 1

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM136

/-! QED-M137: Navier–Stokes blow-up with the force kept away from the singularity
In 2026 OpenAI built a smooth, compactly supported force that drives the 3D Navier–Stokes
equations, started from rest, to blow up in finite time. In that construction the force acts
right where the singularity forms. Can it be done with a force that never acts anywhere near the

x_* ∈ ℝ³ with supp f ∩ (B(x_*,1) × (0,∞)) = ∅ such that the unique smooth solution of
∂ₜu + (u·∇)u + ∇p = νΔu + f, ∇·u = 0, u(·,0) = 0 on ℝ³ × [0,T) satisfies
sup_{t<T} ‖u(t)‖_{L²} < ∞ and limsup_{t↑T} ‖u(t)‖_{L^∞(B(x_*,r))} = ∞ for every r > 0.
(By the scaling u_λ(x,t) = λu(λx,λ²t) the radius 1 can be replaced by any ρ > 0.)
Formalization notes: Space is `Fin 3 → ℝ`; derivatives are Fréchet derivatives (`fderiv`,
`deriv`), so the (sup) norm on `Fin 3 → ℝ` plays no role; Euclidean lengths are written out via
`sqNorm`. The force is C^k for every k on ℝ³ × ℝ and vanishes outside a box
{|xᵢ| ≤ R, δ ≤ t ≤ R} with δ > 0 (compact support in ℝ³ × (0,∞)). "supp f misses B(x_*,1) × (0,∞)"
is encoded as f = 0 on the open ball {|x − x_*| < 1} at all times; since the ball is open this is
equivalent to the closure of {f ≠ 0} not meeting it.
"The unique smooth solution on [0,T)" is encoded as: a pair (u,p), C^k for every k on the open set
ℝ³ × (−∞,T) (values for t < 0 are irrelevant; since f = 0 for t < δ the true solution is 0 there),
satisfying the equations pointwise for 0 < t < T and u(·,0) = 0, in the standard classical
uniqueness class: for every T' < T, u and ∇u are bounded on ℝ³ × [0,T'] and ∫|∇u(t)|² is bounded
on [0,T'], plus finite energy uniformly on [0,T) (the sup_{t<T} ‖u(t)‖_{L²} < ∞ requirement of the
problem), and the pressure is bounded at each time (this excludes harmonic, e.g. linear in x,
pressures acting as a hidden non-decaying force; with it, p is determined up to a function of t by
the velocity and the force, and the energy method gives uniqueness in this class). The local smooth
solution from rest exists and lies in this class up to its maximal time, so exhibiting one such
(u,p) is the same as saying the unique smooth solution behaves as required.
Blow-up at x_*: for every r > 0, u is unbounded on B(x_*,r) × [0,T). As u is continuous on the
compact sets closure(B(x_*,r)) × [0,T'], T' < T, this is exactly limsup_{t↑T}
‖u(t)‖_{L^∞(B(x_*,r))} = ∞. Blow-up elsewhere in addition is not excluded (the problem does not
exclude it).
Viscosity: the claim is stated for every ν > 0. By the scaling v(x,t) = ν⁻¹u(x,t/ν),
q = ν⁻²p, g = ν⁻²f(x,t/ν), which preserves the support condition, the existence for one ν is
equivalent to existence for all ν, so this matches "Let ν > 0".
Proving `Claim` = constructing, for every ν > 0, such a force and a blow-up at a point at distance
≥ 1 from the support of the force. Proving `¬Claim` = showing for some (equivalently every) ν > 0
that no smooth force supported away from a ball can produce a (finite-energy) singularity inside it.

namespace OpenProblems.QEDM137
noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory

/-- Points of ℝ³. -/
abbrev R3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- Squared Euclidean length of a vector in ℝ³. -/
def sqNorm (v : R3) : ℝ := ∑ i : Fin 3, v i ^ 2

/-- Standard basis vector `eᵢ`. -/
def basisVec (i : Fin 3) : R3 := Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)

/-- Spatial partial derivative `∂ᵢ u (x,t)` of a time-dependent vector field. -/
def dx (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (i : Fin 3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun y : R3 => u y t) x (basisVec i)

/-- Spatial Laplacian `Δu (x,t) = ∑ᵢ ∂ᵢ∂ᵢ u`. -/
def lap (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, dx (fun y s => dx u i y s) i x t

/-- Time derivative `∂ₜ u (x,t)`. -/
def dt (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  deriv (fun s : ℝ => u x s) t

/-- Convective term `(u·∇)u (x,t) = ∑ⱼ uⱼ ∂ⱼ u`. -/
def convec (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  ∑ j : Fin 3, (u x t j) • dx u j x t

/-- Spatial gradient of a scalar field. -/
def grad (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : R3 :=
  fun i => fderiv ℝ (fun y : R3 => p y t) x (basisVec i)

/-- Divergence `∇·u (x,t)`. -/
def divg (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, dx u i x t i

/-- `|∇u(x,t)|² = ∑ᵢ |∂ᵢ u(x,t)|²`. -/
def gradSq (u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (x : R3) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, sqNorm (dx u i x t)

/-- `(f,u,p)` is a smooth finite-energy solution from rest of forced Navier–Stokes with viscosity
`ν` on `ℝ³ × [0,T)`, the force vanishes on the unit ball around `xs` at all times, and `u` blows up
at `xs` as `t ↑ T`. -/
def AwayBlowup (ν T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) (xs : R3) : Prop :=
  0 < T ∧
  -- smooth force with compact support in ℝ³ × (0, ∞)
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => f q.1 q.2)) ∧
  (∃ R δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), f x t ≠ 0 →
      (δ ≤ t ∧ t ≤ R ∧ ∀ i : Fin 3, |x i| ≤ R)) ∧
  -- the force never acts in the unit ball around xs
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), sqNorm (x - xs) < 1 → f x t = 0) ∧
  -- smoothness of u and p up to (but excluding) time T
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => u q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R3 × ℝ => p q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  -- the equations on ℝ³ × (0,T)
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → t < T →
      dt u x t + convec u x t + grad p x t = ν • lap u x t + f x t) ∧
  (∀ (x : R3) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → t < T → divg u x t = 0) ∧
  -- start from rest
  (∀ x : R3, u x 0 = 0) ∧
  -- finite energy, uniformly on [0,T)
  (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < T →
      Integrable (fun x : R3 => sqNorm (u x t)) ∧ ∫ x : R3, sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C) ∧
  -- classical uniqueness class on every [0,T'], T' < T
  (∀ T' : ℝ, T' < T → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ T' →
      (∀ x : R3, sqNorm (u x t) ≤ C ∧ gradSq u x t ≤ C) ∧
      Integrable (fun x : R3 => gradSq u x t) ∧ ∫ x : R3, gradSq u x t ≤ C) ∧
  -- pressure bounded at each time (excludes harmonic pressures)
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < T → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : R3, |p x t| ≤ C) ∧
  -- blow-up at xs: u is unbounded on B(xs,r) × [0,T) for every r > 0
  (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ (x : R3) (t : ℝ),
      sqNorm (x - xs) < r ^ 2 ∧ 0 ≤ t ∧ t < T ∧ M < sqNorm (u x t))

/-- For every viscosity there is a forced finite-energy blow-up from rest at a point whose unit
neighbourhood the force never touches. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ ν : ℝ, 0 < ν →
    ∃ (T : ℝ) (f u : R3 → ℝ → R3) (p : R3 → ℝ → ℝ) (xs : R3), AwayBlowup ν T f u p xs

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM137

title: Diameter of the three-pile shuffle group
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Cut a deck of 3n cards into three equal piles and interleave them, choosing any of the 6 orders of the piles at each step. When n is not a power of 3 these moves can produce every (even) arrangement. How many shuffles are needed, in the worst case, to reach every reachable arrangement? Is it of order n log n, as counting suggests, or polynomially larger?
math: For $\sigma\in S_3$ let $g_\sigma\in S_{3n}$ map position $kn+j$ ($k\in\{0,1,2\}$, $0\le j<n$) to $3j+\sigma(k)$, and let $G_{3,3n}=\langle g_\sigma:\sigma\in S_3\rangle$. For $n$ not a power of $3$ (where $G_{3,3n}\supseteq A_{3n}$), let $D(n)$ be the diameter of the (undirected) Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(G_{3,3n},\{g_\sigma^{\pm1}\})$. Counting gives $D(n)=\Omega(n\log n)$. Determine whether $D(n)=O(n\log n)$; failing that, determine the growth exponent $\lim\log D(n)/\log n$ (in particular, prove $D(n)\le n^{C}$ for an absolute $C$).

/-! QED-M138: Diameter of the three-pile shuffle group
Cut a deck of 3n cards into three equal piles and interleave them, choosing any of the 6 orders of the piles at each step. When n is not a power of 3 these moves can produce every (even) arrangement. How many shuffles are needed, in the worst case, to reach every reachable arrangement? Is it of order n log n, as counting suggests, or polynomially larger?
Informal statement: For $\sigma\in S_3$ let $g_\sigma\in S_{3n}$ map position $kn+j$ ($k\in\{0,1,2\}$, $0\le j<n$) to $3j+\sigma(k)$, and let $G_{3,3n}=\langle g_\sigma:\sigma\in S_3\rangle$. Counting gives $D(n)=\Omega(n\log n)$. Determine whether $D(n)=O(n\log n)$; failing that, determine the growth exponent $\lim\log D(n)/\log n$ (in particular, prove $D(n)\le n^{C}$ for an absolute $C$).
Formalization notes:
* Positions are natural numbers; `shuf n σ` is gσ on `[0, 3n)` (position `i = k n + j` with `k = i / n`,
  `j = i % n` goes to `3 j + σ(k)`) and the identity outside, so no `Equiv` proof obligations are needed.
  `shufInv n σ` is its explicit inverse on `[0, 3n)` (`m = 3 j + r ↦ σ⁻¹(r) n + j`). The `Fin 3` casts are exact
  because `i / n < 3` and `m % 3 < 3` for `i, m < 3n`.
* A letter is `(b, σ)`: `b = false` means gσ, `b = true` means gσ⁻¹. `evalWord n w` is the product of the letters
  (as functions). Since the gσ are bijections of a finite set, the group they generate is exactly the set of
  values of words; two group elements are equal iff they agree on `[0, 3n)`.
* `Within n d` says every element of G_{3,3n} is a product of at most `d` letters, i.e. the undirected Cayley graph
  diameter is ≤ d (Cayley graphs are vertex-transitive, so the diameter is the max distance from the identity).
  Judgement call: the Cayley graph is taken undirected (generators and inverses), the standard convention in
  Babai-type diameter questions; the directed diameter is at least as large and the counting lower bound
  Ω(n log n) holds for both.
* `Claim` = the O(n log n) alternative: ∃ C, ∀ n ≥ 2 not a power of 3, D(n) ≤ C · n · ⌊log₂ n⌋.
  (For n ≥ 2, ⌊log₂ n⌋ ≥ 1, so this is exactly D(n) = O(n log n) on that set.) `¬Claim` = D(n)/(n log n) is
  unbounded. The fallback polynomial bound is recorded as `PolyDiameter` but is not part of `Claim`.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM138
noncomputable section

/-- The shuffle `g_σ` on positions `0, …, 3n-1` (identity on larger positions). -/
def shuf (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if i < 3 * n then 3 * (i % n) + ((σ (⟨(i / n) % 3, Nat.mod_lt _ (by norm_num)⟩ : Fin 3) : Fin 3) : ℕ) else i

/-- The inverse shuffle `g_σ⁻¹` on positions `0, …, 3n-1` (identity on larger positions). -/
def shufInv (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (m : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if m < 3 * n then n * ((σ.symm (⟨m % 3, Nat.mod_lt _ (by norm_num)⟩ : Fin 3) : Fin 3) : ℕ) + m / 3 else m

/-- A letter: a generator `g_σ` (`false`) or its inverse (`true`). -/
abbrev Letter : Type := Bool × Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)

/-- The permutation (as a function) represented by a letter. -/
def letterFun (n : ℕ) (a : Letter) : ℕ → ℕ :=
  cond a.1 (shufInv n a.2) (shuf n a.2)

/-- The product of a word of letters. -/
def evalWord (n : ℕ) : List Letter → ℕ → ℕ
  | [] => id
  | a :: w => letterFun n a ∘ evalWord n w

/-- Every element of `G_{3,3n}` has word length at most `d`, i.e. `D(n) ≤ d`. -/
def Within (n d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : List Letter, ∃ w' : List Letter, w'.length ≤ d ∧
    ∀ i : ℕ, i < 3 * n → evalWord n w' i = evalWord n w i

/-- Fallback target (not the Claim): polynomial diameter. -/
def PolyDiameter : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → (¬ ∃ k : ℕ, n = 3 ^ k) → Within n (n ^ C)

/-- `D(n) = O(n log n)` for `n` not a power of `3`. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → (¬ ∃ k : ℕ, n = 3 ^ k) → Within n (C * n * Nat.log 2 n)

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM138

to 1. Proving `Claim` = the statement for every θ < 1; proving `¬Claim` = some θ < 1 for which
only finitely many such n exist.
-/

noncomputable section

/-- Largest prime factor of `m` (0 for `m ≤ 1`). -/

/-- For every θ < 1, infinitely many n have P(n), P(n+1), P(n+2) all exceeding n^θ. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ θ : ℝ, θ < 1 →
    Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (n : ℝ) ^ θ < (lpf n : ℝ) ∧ (n : ℝ) ^ θ < (lpf (n + 1) : ℝ) ∧

title: Least volume of a Kakeya set for discs
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: A set in space contains a flat unit disc in every orientation. How small can its volume be? Such sets cannot have zero volume, unlike sets containing a needle in every direction.
math: For a unit vector ν let D_ν = {x ∈ ℝ³ : x·ν = 0, |x| ≤ 1}, and c_* = inf{|E| : E ⊂ ℝ³ compact, ∀ν ∃x_ν, x_ν + D_ν ⊂ E} (c_* > 0 by Marstrand/Falconer). Decide whether c_* < (4/3)π, i.e. whether some compact set containing a translate of every D_ν has smaller volume than the unit ball. (Determining c_* exactly and whether the infimum is attained are further questions.)

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M140: Least volume of a Kakeya set for discs
A set in space contains a flat unit disc in every orientation. How small can its volume be? Such sets
cannot have zero volume, unlike sets containing a needle in every direction.
Informal statement: For a unit vector ν let D_ν = {x ∈ ℝ³ : x·ν = 0, |x| ≤ 1}. Let
c_* = inf{|E| : E ⊂ ℝ³ compact, ∀ν ∃x_ν, x_ν + D_ν ⊂ E}. By Marstrand and Falconer's L² bound for the
2-plane maximal operator, c_* > 0. Determine c_*. The Claim formalized here is the sharp sub-question
"is the unit ball beaten?": c_* < (4/3)π, i.e. there is a compact set containing a translate of every
D_ν whose Lebesgue measure is less than that of the unit ball.
Formalization notes: ℝ³ is modelled as `Fin 3 → ℝ` with its product Lebesgue measure `volume`; the
Euclidean structure is written out explicitly (dot product `∑ i, x i * ν i`, squared norm `∑ i, x i ^ 2`),
avoiding the sup-norm that Mathlib puts on `Fin 3 → ℝ`. A set E is a "disc Kakeya set" if it is compact
and for every unit vector ν some translate x + D_ν lies in E. Since c_* is an infimum over these sets
and the unit ball (all x_ν = 0) is admissible with volume 4π/3, "c_* < 4π/3" is equivalent to the
existence of an admissible E with volume < 4π/3, which is how `Claim` is stated (no `sInf` needed).
Proving `Claim` = exhibiting a disc Kakeya set beating the ball; `¬Claim` = the ball is optimal
(c_* = 4π/3, attained). The other sub-questions (exact value of c_* if < 4π/3; whether the infimum is
attained) are not captured by this Claim.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM140

noncomputable section

/-- Euclidean dot product on `ℝ³ = Fin 3 → ℝ`. -/
def dot (x y : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i : Fin 3, x i * y i

/-- The unit disc through the origin perpendicular to `ν`. -/
def disc (ν : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ) :=
  {y | dot y ν = 0 ∧ dot y y ≤ 1}

/-- `E` is compact and contains a translate of the unit disc perpendicular to every unit vector. -/
def IsDiscKakeya (E : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  IsCompact E ∧ ∀ ν : Fin 3 → ℝ, dot ν ν = 1 → ∃ x : Fin 3 → ℝ, ∀ y ∈ disc ν, x + y ∈ E

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ E : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ), IsDiscKakeya E ∧
    MeasureTheory.volume E < ENNReal.ofReal (4 / 3 * Real.pi)

end

end OpenProblems.QEDM140

title: Forced blow-up for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: The surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equation is a 2D model of geophysical flow. Whether it can blow up from smooth data is a famous open problem. Can at least a smooth, compactly supported push, applied to a fluid that starts at rest, make it blow up in finite time, as was done for 3D Navier–Stokes in 2026?
math: Consider inviscid SQG on R^2: d_t theta + u.grad theta = f, u = grad^perp (-Delta)^{-1/2} theta, theta(.,0)=0. Decide whether there is f in C_c^infty(R^2 x (0,infty)) whose unique smooth solution on [0,T) satisfies limsup_{t->T} ||grad theta(t)||_{L^infty} = infty for some T < infty. (Variant, not part of the formal Claim: the same for supercritical dissipative SQG, + kappa(-Delta)^{alpha/2} theta with 0<alpha<1; for alpha>=1 smooth forcing gives global regularity.)

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M141: Forced blow-up for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation
The surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equation is a 2D model of geophysical flow. Whether it can
blow up from smooth data is a famous open problem. Can at least a smooth, compactly supported push,
applied to a fluid that starts at rest, make it blow up in finite time, as was done for 3D
Navier–Stokes in 2026?
Informal statement: Consider inviscid SQG on ℝ²: ∂ₜθ + u·∇θ = f, u = ∇^⊥(−Δ)^{−1/2}θ,
θ(·,0) = 0. Decide whether there is f ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ² × (0,∞)) whose unique smooth solution on [0,T)
satisfies limsup_{t↑T} ‖∇θ(t)‖_{L^∞} = ∞ for some T < ∞. (Variant, not part of `Claim`: the same
for supercritical dissipative SQG, + κ(−Δ)^{α/2}θ with 0 < α < 1.)
Formalization notes: Space is `Fin 2 → ℝ` with Lebesgue measure; derivatives are Fréchet
derivatives, and the Euclidean length is written out (`eucl`), so the sup norm on `Fin 2 → ℝ`
plays no role. Velocity: ∇^⊥ = (−∂₂, ∂₁) and (−Δ)^{−1/2} on ℝ² is the Riesz potential with kernel
1/(2π|x|). For θ(·,t) smooth and compactly supported, ∂ⱼ(−Δ)^{−1/2}θ = (−Δ)^{−1/2}∂ⱼθ, so
u(x,t) = (1/2π) (−∫ ∂₂θ(y,t)/|x−y| dy, ∫ ∂₁θ(y,t)/|x−y| dy); these integrals converge absolutely
(|·|⁻¹ is locally integrable in 2D), so there is no principal value and no Bochner junk. (The other
sign convention u = −∇^⊥Λ⁻¹θ is equivalent via the reflection x₁ ↦ −x₁, which maps C_c^∞ forces to
C_c^∞ forces.)
"The unique smooth solution on [0,T)": θ is C^k for every k on the open set ℝ² × (−∞,T) (values for
t < 0 irrelevant), θ(·,0) = 0, the equation holds pointwise for 0 < t < T, and for every T' < T the
supports of θ(·,t), t ∈ [0,T'], lie in a fixed bounded set. The true solution has this property
(θ is transported by a bounded smooth velocity and the force has compact support), and smooth
solutions in this class are unique (Lipschitz velocity, Riesz transforms bounded on L², energy
estimate for the difference), so exhibiting one such θ is the same as speaking of "the" solution.
The force is C^k for all k on ℝ² × ℝ and vanishes outside a box {|xᵢ| ≤ R, δ ≤ t ≤ R}, δ > 0.
Blow-up: ∇θ is unbounded on ℝ² × [0,T). Because θ is smooth with uniformly bounded support on each
[0,T'], T' < T, ∇θ is bounded there, so this is exactly limsup_{t↑T} ‖∇θ(t)‖_{L^∞} = ∞ (and the
solution genuinely cannot be continued smoothly past T). |∂₁θ| + |∂₂θ| is equivalent to |∇θ|.
Proving `Claim` = constructing a smooth compactly supported force and finite-time gradient blow-up
from rest. Proving `¬Claim` = global regularity of forced inviscid SQG from rest for every such
force (which would imply global regularity for all smooth compactly supported unforced data).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM141
noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory

/-- Points of ℝ². -/
abbrev R2 : Type := Fin 2 → ℝ

/-- Euclidean length in ℝ². -/
def eucl (v : R2) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (v 0 ^ 2 + v 1 ^ 2)

/-- Spatial partial derivative `∂ᵢθ(x,t)` of a time-dependent scalar field. -/
def pd (θ : R2 → ℝ → ℝ) (i : Fin 2) (x : R2) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun y : R2 => θ y t) x (Pi.single i (1 : ℝ))

/-- Time derivative `∂ₜθ(x,t)`. -/
def dt (θ : R2 → ℝ → ℝ) (x : R2) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  deriv (fun s : ℝ => θ x s) t

/-- SQG velocity `u = ∇^⊥(−Δ)^{−1/2}θ = (−∂₂ψ, ∂₁ψ)` with `ψ = θ * (2π|·|)⁻¹`,
written as `∂ⱼψ = (∂ⱼθ) * (2π|·|)⁻¹`. -/
def vel (θ : R2 → ℝ → ℝ) (x : R2) (t : ℝ) : Fin 2 → ℝ := fun i =>
  if i = 0 then
    -((1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * ∫ y : R2, pd θ 1 y t / eucl (x - y))
  else
    (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * ∫ y : R2, pd θ 0 y t / eucl (x - y)

/-- `(f, θ)` is a smooth solution from rest of forced inviscid SQG on `ℝ² × [0,T)` whose gradient
blows up as `t ↑ T`. -/
def SQGBlowup (f : R2 → ℝ → ℝ) (T : ℝ) (θ : R2 → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < T ∧
  -- smooth force with compact support in ℝ² × (0, ∞)
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k (fun q : R2 × ℝ => f q.1 q.2)) ∧
  (∃ R δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (x : R2) (t : ℝ), f x t ≠ 0 →
      (δ ≤ t ∧ t ≤ R ∧ ∀ i : Fin 2, |x i| ≤ R)) ∧
  -- smooth solution up to (but excluding) time T
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ k (fun q : R2 × ℝ => θ q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Iio T)) ∧
  -- start from rest
  (∀ x : R2, θ x 0 = 0) ∧
  -- uniformly compact spatial support on every [0,T'], T' < T
  (∀ T' : ℝ, T' < T → ∃ R : ℝ, ∀ (x : R2) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ T' → θ x t ≠ 0 →
      ∀ i : Fin 2, |x i| ≤ R) ∧
  -- the equation on ℝ² × (0,T)
  (∀ (x : R2) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → t < T →
      dt θ x t + ∑ i : Fin 2, vel θ x t i * pd θ i x t = f x t) ∧
  -- gradient blow-up: ∇θ unbounded on ℝ² × [0,T)
  (∀ M : ℝ, ∃ (x : R2) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t ∧ t < T ∧ M < |pd θ 0 x t| + |pd θ 1 x t|)

/-- Some smooth compactly supported force drives inviscid SQG from rest to finite-time blow-up. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : R2 → ℝ → ℝ) (T : ℝ) (θ : R2 → ℝ → ℝ), SQGBlowup f T θ

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM141

title: Lonely runner with speeds at most 2n
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Tao proved the lonely runner conjecture when every speed is at most 1.2 times the number of runners. Push this to speeds at most twice the number of runners (and ideally any fixed multiple).
math: For distinct positive integers v_1,…,v_n let δ(v) = sup_{t∈ℝ} min_i ‖t v_i‖, where ‖·‖ is distance to the nearest integer. Prove that δ(v) ≥ 1/(n+1) for every n ≥ 1 and all distinct v_1,…,v_n ∈ {1,…,2n}. (Tao 2018, Prop. 1.5, proves this for speeds ≤ ⌊6n/5⌋; conjecturally there is no speed restriction.)

title: Hats on a flat torus: how much must be left uncovered?
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: The hat tile can cover the plane, but never in a repeating pattern, so copies of the hat can never exactly cover a flat torus (a doughnut-shaped surface that is flat, like a video-game screen that wraps around). Packing hats on a torus of area A always leaves some area uncovered. Show that the least uncovered area grows without bound as A grows, and find how fast it grows. Cutting a square out of a hat tiling shows it is at most a constant times the square root of A.
math: Let $H$ be the hat polykite (area normalised to $1$); copies may be rotated and reflected. For a lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^2$ of covolume $A$, a packing of $T_\Lambda=\mathbb R^2/\Lambda$ is a finite family of isometric copies of $H$ in $T_\Lambda$ with disjoint interiors (each copy embedded). Let $g(A)=\inf_{\Lambda:\,\mathrm{covol}(\Lambda)=A}\ \inf_{\text{packings}}\ \big(A-\#\text{copies}\big)$. Trivially $g(A)=O(\sqrt A)$. (i) Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ as $A\to\infty$. (ii) Determine the order of growth of $g$; in particular, is $g(A)\asymp\sqrt A$?

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M143: Hats on a flat torus: how much must be left uncovered?
The hat tile can cover the plane, but never in a repeating pattern, so copies of the hat can never exactly cover a flat torus (a doughnut-shaped surface that is flat, like a video-game screen that wraps around). Packing hats on a torus of area A always leaves some area uncovered. Show that the least uncovered area grows without bound as A grows, and find how fast it grows. Cutting a square out of a hat tiling shows it is at most a constant times the square root of A.
Informal statement: Let $H$ be the hat polykite (area normalised to $1$); copies may be rotated and reflected. For a lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^2$ of covolume $A$, a packing of $T_\Lambda=\mathbb R^2/\Lambda$ is a finite family of isometric copies of $H$ in $T_\Lambda$ with disjoint interiors (each copy embedded). Let $g(A)=\inf_{\Lambda:\,\mathrm{covol}(\Lambda)=A}\ \inf_{\text{packings}}\ \big(A-\#\text{copies}\big)$. Trivially $g(A)=O(\sqrt A)$. (i) Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ as $A\to\infty$. (ii) Determine the order of growth of $g$; in particular, is $g(A)\asymp\sqrt A$?
Formalization notes:
* Hat: the 8-kite union in hex coordinates `(a,b) ↦ a + b/2 + i(√3/2) b` (same encoding as QED-E096), of area
  `8√3` (each kite has area √3). Instead of normalising the area to 1 we keep this hat and measure the uncovered
  area as `A − N · 8√3`. Rescaling the plane by `(8√3)^{−1/2}` shows `g_here(A) = 8√3 · g(A / (8√3))`, so (i) and
  the order of growth in (ii) are unchanged.
* Lattice Λ = ℤu + ℤv with `u, v ∈ ℂ`, covolume `|Re u · Im v − Im u · Re v|` (> 0 iff u, v independent).
* Packing of the torus by N hats ⇔ Λ-periodic packing of the plane with N orbits: isometries `g₀, …, g_{N−1}` of ℂ
  (reflections allowed) such that the translates `gᵢ(H) + m u + n v` (i < N, m, n ∈ ℤ) have pairwise disjoint
  interiors for distinct indices `(i, m, n)`. Disjointness of `gᵢ(H)` from its own nonzero Λ-translates is exactly
  "each copy is embedded in the torus"; disjointness across different i is the packing condition. The copies on
  the torus are the images of the gᵢ(H), so #copies = N and the uncovered area is `A − 8√3 · N`.
* `Claim` = part (i): for every M there is A₀ such that every packing of every torus of covolume ≥ A₀ leaves
  uncovered area > M, i.e. g(A) → ∞. (Degenerate lattices have covolume 0 and are excluded once A₀ > 0.)
  `¬Claim` = bounded defect along a sequence of tori with covolume → ∞. Part (ii)'s √A lower bound is recorded as
  `SqrtDefect`, not part of `Claim` (the O(√A) upper bound is the known trivial bound).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM143
noncomputable section

/-- Hex-grid point `(a, b) ↦ a + b/2 + i·(√3/2)·b`. -/
def hexPt (a b : ℤ) : ℂ := ⟨(a : ℝ) + (b : ℝ) / 2, Real.sqrt 3 / 2 * (b : ℝ)⟩

/-- A kite with the given four grid vertices. -/
def kite (p q r s : ℤ × ℤ) : Set ℂ :=
  convexHull ℝ {hexPt p.1 p.2, hexPt q.1 q.2, hexPt r.1 r.2, hexPt s.1 s.2}

/-- The hat monotile, as a union of 8 kites. -/
def hat : Set ℂ :=
  kite (0, 0) (2, -1) (2, 0) (1, 1) ∪ kite (0, 0) (1, 1) (0, 2) (-1, 2) ∪
  kite (0, 0) (-1, -1) (0, -2) (1, -2) ∪ kite (0, 0) (1, -2) (2, -2) (2, -1) ∪
  kite (4, -2) (5, -1) (4, 0) (3, 0) ∪ kite (4, -2) (3, 0) (2, 0) (2, -1) ∪
  kite (2, 2) (0, 3) (0, 2) (1, 1) ∪ kite (2, 2) (1, 1) (2, 0) (3, 0)

/-- Area of the hat. -/
def hatArea : ℝ := 8 * Real.sqrt 3

/-- Covolume of the lattice `ℤu + ℤv`. -/
def covol (u v : ℂ) : ℝ := |u.re * v.im - u.im * v.re|

/-- Translate of a set by the lattice vector `m u + n v`. -/
def ltrans (u v : ℂ) (m n : ℤ) (X : Set ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  (fun z : ℂ => z + ((m : ℂ) * u + (n : ℂ) * v)) '' X

/-- `N` hats `g i '' hat` form a packing of the torus `ℂ / (ℤu + ℤv)`. -/
def IsTorusPacking (u v : ℂ) (N : ℕ) (g : Fin N → (ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Fin N, ∀ m n m' n' : ℤ, (i, m, n) ≠ (j, m', n') →
    Disjoint (interior (ltrans u v m n (g i '' hat))) (interior (ltrans u v m' n' (g j '' hat)))

/-- Uncovered area of a packing of `N` hats on a torus with periods `u, v`. -/
def defect (u v : ℂ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ := covol u v - (N : ℝ) * hatArea

/-- Part (ii) lower bound, not part of `Claim`: `g(A) ≥ c √A` for large `A`. -/
def SqrtDefect : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ A₀ : ℝ, ∀ u v : ℂ, A₀ ≤ covol u v →
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (g : Fin N → (ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ)), IsTorusPacking u v N g →
      c * Real.sqrt (covol u v) ≤ defect u v N

/-- Part (i): the least uncovered area tends to infinity with the area of the torus. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ A₀ : ℝ, ∀ u v : ℂ, A₀ ≤ covol u v →
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (g : Fin N → (ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ)), IsTorusPacking u v N g → M < defect u v N

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM143

/-! QED-M144: Joint residues of the largest prime factors of n and n+1
Let P(n) be the largest prime factor of n. Show that the last digits of P(n) and P(n+1) behave like
two independent fair choices from {1,3,7,9}: each of the 16 pairs occurs for asymptotically 1/16 of
all n. More generally, for any modulus q, the pair (P(n) mod q, P(n+1) mod q) should be uniform over
pairs of reduced residues.

a, b ∈ (ℤ/qℤ)^×, the natural density of {n ≥ 2 : P(n) ≡ a, P(n+1) ≡ b (mod q)} equals φ(q)⁻².

prime factor (only n ≥ 2 are counted, so the junk value lpf 1 = 0 never enters). Residues are taken
by casting to `ZMod q`; "reduced residue" is `IsUnit` in `ZMod q`, and φ is `Nat.totient`.
Natural density is the limit of (1/x)·#{2 ≤ n ≤ x : …} as x → ∞ through the naturals (equivalent
to through the reals, since the count is a step function). `Claim` is the general modulus-q
statement; the mod-10 headline is its case q = 10 (φ(10) = 4), and `Claim10` records it
separately. Proving `Claim` = equidistribution for every q; proving `¬Claim` = some q, a, b for
which the density fails to exist or differs from φ(q)⁻².

namespace OpenProblems.QEDM144
noncomputable section

open Filter Topology

/-- Largest prime factor of `m` (0 for `m ≤ 1`). -/
def lpf (m : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.primeFactors m).sup id

/-- `#{2 ≤ n ≤ x : P(n) ≡ a, P(n+1) ≡ b (mod q)}`. -/
def count (q : ℕ) (a b : ZMod q) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Set.ncard {n : ℕ | 2 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ x ∧ ((lpf n : ℕ) : ZMod q) = a ∧ ((lpf (n + 1) : ℕ) : ZMod q) = b}

/-- The mod-10 headline: each of the 16 pairs of last digits has density 1/16. -/
def Claim10 : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : ℕ, a ∈ ({1, 3, 7, 9} : Finset ℕ) → b ∈ ({1, 3, 7, 9} : Finset ℕ) →
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (count 10 (a : ZMod 10) (b : ZMod 10) x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop
      (𝓝 (1 / 16 : ℝ))

/-- Joint equidistribution of `(P(n) mod q, P(n+1) mod q)` over pairs of reduced residues. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ q : ℕ, 2 ≤ q → ∀ a b : ZMod q, IsUnit a → IsUnit b →
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (count q a b x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop
      (𝓝 (1 / ((Nat.totient q : ℝ) ^ 2)))

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM144

title: Primes with equal binary and ternary digit sums

title: Largest prime factor of p−1 in residue classes
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: For each prime p, take the largest prime factor of p − 1. Show that this factor is 1 mod 4 for half of all primes and 3 mod 4 for the other half. More generally, show it is spread evenly over the allowed residue classes mod q.
math: Let $P(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. Prove that for every fixed $q\ge2$ and every $a$ with $\gcd(a,q)=1$, $\#\{p\le x:\ P(p-1)\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\}\sim\frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}$ as $x\to\infty$. The first open case is $q=4$, $a=1$: $\#\{p\le x: P(p-1)\equiv1\ (4)\}\sim\tfrac12\pi(x)$.

/-! QED-M147: Largest prime factor of p−1 in residue classes
For each prime p, take the largest prime factor of p − 1. Show that this factor is 1 mod 4 for half of all primes and 3 mod 4 for the other half. More generally, show it is spread evenly over the allowed residue classes mod q.
Informal statement: Let $P(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. Prove that for every fixed $q\ge2$ and every $a$ with $\gcd(a,q)=1$, $\#\{p\le x:\ P(p-1)\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\}\sim\frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}$ as $x\to\infty$. The first open case is $q=4$, $a=1$: $\#\{p\le x: P(p-1)\equiv1\ (4)\}\sim\tfrac12\pi(x)$.
Formalization notes: P(n) = largest prime factor, `gpf n = max 1 (sup of n.primeFactors)`, so P(1) = 1 (only
p = 2 has p − 1 = 1; a single prime does not affect the asymptotic). x ranges over ℕ (the counts only change at
integers). `countRes q a x` = #{p ≤ x prime : P(p − 1) ≡ a (mod q)}, written as `gpf (p-1) % q = a % q`
(truncated subtraction is harmless since p ≥ 2). The asymptotic `count ∼ π(x)/φ(q)` is stated as
`count / π(x) → 1/φ(q)`, which is equivalent because π(x) > 0 for x ≥ 2 and φ(q) ≥ 1 (the ratio's junk value
for x < 2 does not affect the limit). `Nat.primeCounting x` = π(x), `Nat.totient` = φ. `Claim` = the
asymptotic for all q ≥ 2 and all a coprime to q; `¬Claim` = it fails for some (q, a), e.g. a persistent bias
for q = 4.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM147
noncomputable section

/-- Largest prime factor of `n`, with `gpf 0 = gpf 1 = 1`. -/
def gpf (n : ℕ) : ℕ := max 1 (n.primeFactors.sup id)

/-- `#{p ≤ x prime : P(p - 1) ≡ a (mod q)}`. -/
def countRes (q a x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range (x + 1)).filter (fun p : ℕ => p.Prime ∧ gpf (p - 1) % q = a % q)).card

/-- `P(p - 1)` is equidistributed among the reduced residue classes mod `q`. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ q a : ℕ, 2 ≤ q → Nat.Coprime a q →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (countRes q a x : ℝ) / (Nat.primeCounting x : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (Nat.totient q : ℝ)))

end
end OpenProblems.QEDM147

title: Critical Ising interfaces on the hat tiling converge to SLE(3)
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Put an Ising spin on every tile of a hat tiling, with neighbouring tiles (sharing an edge segment) interacting, at the critical temperature. Take a large simply connected region with plus spins forced on one boundary arc and minus spins on the other. Show that, as the tiles shrink, the interface between the plus and minus clusters converges to the random curve SLE(3), just as on the square lattice, although the hat graph is neither periodic nor isoradial.
math: Let $G_T$ be the tile-adjacency graph of a hat tiling $T$ (Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss hat, reflections allowed; tiles adjacent iff they share a boundary segment of positive length), with the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour Ising model, $J\equiv1$. Prove: (i) there is $\beta_c\in(0,\infty)$, independent of $T$, such that the plus-state magnetisation of every tile vanishes for $0<\beta\le\beta_c$ and is positive for $\beta>\beta_c$; (ii) for every hat tiling $T$, every Jordan domain $\Omega$ with distinct boundary points $a,b$, and all discretisations $(\Omega_\delta,a_\delta,b_\delta)$ by simply connected unions of tiles of $\delta T$ whose boundary curves converge to $\partial\Omega$ uniformly up to reparametrisation, with $a_\delta\to a$, $b_\delta\to b$: with Dobrushin boundary conditions ($+$ on the boundary arc from $a_\delta$ to $b_\delta$, $-$ on the other) at $\beta=\beta_c$, the interface from $a_\delta$ to $b_\delta$ (any interface path, whatever choice is made at vertices where several interface edges meet) converges in law, in the topology of curves up to reparametrisation, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_3$ in $(\Omega,a,b)$.

import Mathlib
/-! QED-M148: Critical Ising interfaces on the hat tiling converge to SLE(3)
Put an Ising spin on every tile of a hat tiling, with neighbouring tiles (sharing an edge segment) interacting, at the critical temperature. Take a large simply connected region with plus spins forced on one boundary arc and minus spins on the other. Show that, as the tiles shrink, the interface between the plus and minus clusters converges to the random curve SLE(3), just as on the square lattice, although the hat graph is neither periodic nor isoradial.
Informal statement: Let $G_T$ be the tile-adjacency graph of a hat tiling $T$ (Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss hat, reflections allowed; tiles adjacent iff they share a boundary segment of positive length), with the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour Ising model, $J\equiv1$. Prove: (i) there is $\beta_c\in(0,\infty)$, independent of $T$, such that the plus-state magnetisation of every tile vanishes for $0<\beta\le\beta_c$ and is positive for $\beta>\beta_c$; (ii) for every hat tiling $T$, every Jordan domain $\Omega$ with distinct boundary points $a,b$, and all discretisations $(\Omega_\delta,a_\delta,b_\delta)$ by simply connected unions of tiles of $\delta T$ whose boundary curves converge to $\partial\Omega$ uniformly up to reparametrisation, with $a_\delta\to a$, $b_\delta\to b$: with Dobrushin boundary conditions ($+$ on the boundary arc from $a_\delta$ to $b_\delta$, $-$ on the other) at $\beta=\beta_c$, the interface from $a_\delta$ to $b_\delta$ (any interface path, whatever choice is made at vertices where several interface edges meet) converges in law, in the topology of curves up to reparametrisation, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_3$ in $(\Omega,a,b)$.
Formalization notes:
* Hat tilings, as in the AKLT problem of the same batch: the hat polygon (lattice coordinates from
  Kaplan's `hatviz`, checked: area `8√3` = 8 kites) as a union of 11 closed triangles; a tiling is a
  set of isometric copies (`ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ`, reflections allowed) covering `ℂ` with disjoint interiors.
  `Vert` = points in ≥ 3 tiles; `ArcOf 𝒯 A B u w` = `u, w` are the ends of a common boundary arc
  of the distinct tiles `A, B` (same connected component of `A ∩ B`). Tiles are Ising sites;
  `tAdj A B` iff `A ∩ B` is infinite, i.e. they share a segment of positive length (two polygons
  with disjoint interiors meet in finitely many points otherwise).
* (i) Critical point. Plus-state magnetisation at tile `x`: `⟨σ_x⟩^+_Λ` in finite `Λ ∋ x` with all
  tiles outside `Λ` fixed to `+` (each outside neighbour contributes field 1). By GKS it is
  non-increasing in `Λ`, so the infinite-volume value is the infimum over finite `Λ ∋ x`
  (`mPlus`). The problem allowed assuming or proving the existence of a `T`-independent `β_c`; we
  require proving it (asserted inside `Claim` with `∃ β_c`), which avoids an implication that
  would be vacuous if no such `β_c` existed.
* Domain. A Jordan domain with two marked points is given by `f`, continuous and injective on the
  closed unit disc and holomorphic on the open disc (Carathéodory: every Jordan domain arises so),
  `Ω = f(𝔻)`, `a = f(-1)`, `b = f(1)`. Restricting from general bounded simply connected domains
  with Carathéodory convergence to Jordan domains with uniform (Fréchet) convergence of boundary
  curves is the one sharpening made; by Radó's theorem this convergence implies Carathéodory
  convergence with the marked points converging as prime ends, so it is a special case of the
  original.
* Discrete domain (`DiscDomain`, `IsDisc`), in units of the unscaled tiling `𝒯` (positions are
  multiplied by `δ`): a finite set `D` of tiles and a simple cycle `v_0, …, v_{L+2}` of vertices
  that lists every boundary edge (arc between a tile in `D` and one outside) exactly as consecutive
  pairs; hence `D` is the set of tiles enclosed by a simple closed curve (simply connected).
  `a = v_0`, `b = v_j`. Dobrushin boundary condition per boundary arc: `+1` on arcs
  `v_i v_{i+1}` with `i < j`, else `-1` (edge-based, so a tile meeting both arcs is not ambiguous).
  Energy: `-Σ_{tAdj pairs in D} σσ' - Σ_{boundary arcs} σ_{inner tile}·bc`. Convergence: the
  closed polygon through `δ v_i` is `ε`-close to `s ↦ f(e^{2πis})` after an increasing or
  decreasing reparametrisation of the circle, and `δ v_0 → a`, `δ v_j → b`. Replacing arcs by
  chords moves curves by `O(δ)`, which is invisible in the limit.
* Interface. A disagreement edge joins `u, w` along an arc of tiles `A ∈ D` and `B` where the
  spins differ (for `B ∉ D` the "spin" of `B` is the boundary value). All vertices other than
  `a, b` meet an even number of disagreement edges, `a, b` an odd number, so trails from `a` to
  `b` (walks using each edge at most once) exist. At vertices where 4 or more interface edges meet
  the interface is ambiguous; `Claim` requires convergence for every selection rule `sel` (any
  deterministic choice of a valid trail per configuration). The curve is the
  polygon through `δ`·(trail vertices), parametrised by `[0,1]`.
* Convergence in law in the space of curves modulo increasing reparametrisation (metric
  `reparamDist`): by the portmanteau theorem it suffices, and is necessary, to have convergence of
  expectations of all `F` with `|F| ≤ 1` that are 1-Lipschitz for `reparamDist` (such `F` are
  reparametrisation-invariant; bounded Lipschitz functions on the subspace of continuous curves
  extend to all functions with the same bounds, so quantifying over functions on all maps
  `[0,1] → ℂ` is equivalent).
* SLE₃. A process `W` is `√κ·`(standard Brownian motion) if `W_0 = 0`, its paths are continuous
  on `[0,∞)`, and the increments over any partition `0 = τ_0 < … < τ_k` are independent centred
  Gaussians with variances `κ(τ_{i+1} - τ_i)` (joint law = product measure). A curve `η` in `ℍ`
  from `0` is driven by `W` if it is simple, `η(t) ∈ ℍ` for `t > 0`, and for each `t` there is a
  conformal map `g_t : ℍ \ η(0,t] → ℍ` with hydrodynamic normalisation
  `g_t(z) = z + 2t/z + o(1/z)` (half-plane capacity parametrisation) and `g_t(η(t)) = W_t` as a
  boundary limit. This is the Loewner characterisation; for `κ = 3 ≤ 4` the SLE trace is a.s. a
  simple curve (Rohde–Schramm), so this describes chordal SLE₃ in `ℍ`, which is transient
  (`|η(t)| → ∞`). The curve in `(Ω, a, b)` is `f ∘ m ∘ η` with `m(z) = (z - i)/(z + i)`
  (`ℍ → 𝔻`, `0 ↦ -1`, `∞ ↦ 1`), reparametrised to `[0,1]`; this law does not depend on the choice
  of `f` (scale invariance of SLE). `IsSLE3Setup` asks for a probability space with such `W` and a
  Borel-measurable random continuous curve `Γ` that is a.s. this curve; `Claim` asserts such a
  setup exists (no vacuity) and the convergence holds for every one.
* Proving `Claim` = (i) and (ii). Proving `¬Claim` = no `T`-independent critical point, or failure
  of convergence for some hat tiling, Jordan domain, discretisation and interface selection.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDM148
noncomputable section
open scoped Classical
open MeasureTheory Filter Topology

/-- The point `x + y·e^{iπ/3}` of the triangular lattice. -/
def hp (x y : ℤ) : ℂ := ⟨(x : ℝ) + (y : ℝ) / 2, Real.sqrt 3 / 2 * (y : ℝ)⟩

/-- A triangulation (11 triangles) of the hat polygon with vertices, in lattice coordinates,
(0,0),(-1,-1),(0,-2),(2,-2),(2,-1),(4,-2),(5,-1),(4,0),(3,0),(2,2),(0,3),(0,2),(-1,2). -/
def hatTriangles : List ((ℤ × ℤ) × (ℤ × ℤ) × (ℤ × ℤ)) :=
  [((0, 0), (-1, -1), (0, -2)), ((0, 0), (0, -2), (2, -2)), ((-1, 2), (0, 0), (2, -2)),
   ((-1, 2), (2, -2), (2, -1)), ((-1, 2), (2, -1), (4, -2)), ((4, -2), (5, -1), (4, 0)),
   ((4, -2), (4, 0), (3, 0)), ((-1, 2), (4, -2), (3, 0)), ((3, 0), (2, 2), (0, 3)),
   ((3, 0), (0, 3), (0, 2)), ((3, 0), (0, 2), (-1, 2))]

/-- The closed hat tile (Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss), as the union of the closed
triangles of a triangulation of its boundary polygon. -/
def hat : Set ℂ :=
  ⋃ t ∈ hatTriangles,
    convexHull ℝ ({hp t.1.1 t.1.2, hp t.2.1.1 t.2.1.2, hp t.2.2.1 t.2.2.2} : Set ℂ)

/-- `𝒯` is a hat tiling of the plane: every tile is an isometric copy of the hat (reflections
allowed), the tiles cover `ℂ`, and distinct tiles have disjoint interiors. -/
def IsHatTiling (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ A ∈ 𝒯, ∃ g : ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ, A = g '' hat) ∧
  ⋃₀ 𝒯 = Set.univ ∧
  (∀ A ∈ 𝒯, ∀ B ∈ 𝒯, A ≠ B → interior A ∩ interior B = ∅)

/-- Vertices of the tiling graph: points lying in at least three tiles. -/
def Vert (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) : Set ℂ := {p : ℂ | (3 : ℕ∞) ≤ {A : Set ℂ | A ∈ 𝒯 ∧ p ∈ A}.encard}

/-- `u, w` are joined by an edge of the tiling graph along the common boundary of tiles `A ≠ B`:
both are vertices and lie in the same connected component of `A ∩ B` (a common boundary arc;
interior points of such an arc lie in exactly two tiles, so its endpoints are consecutive
vertices). -/
def ArcOf (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) (A B : Set ℂ) (u w : ℂ) : Prop :=
  u ∈ Vert 𝒯 ∧ w ∈ Vert 𝒯 ∧ u ≠ w ∧ A ≠ B ∧ w ∈ connectedComponentIn (A ∩ B) u

/-- The planar graph `G_𝒯` on the vertex set of the tiling. -/
def tilingGraph (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) : SimpleGraph (Vert 𝒯) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u w : Vert 𝒯 => ∃ A ∈ 𝒯, ∃ B ∈ 𝒯, ArcOf 𝒯 A B u.1 w.1)

/-! ### Ising model on tiles -/

/-- Tiles sharing a boundary segment of positive length. -/
def tAdj (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) (A B : 𝒯) : Prop := A ≠ B ∧ (A.1 ∩ B.1).Infinite

/-- Spin value `±1`. -/
def spinv (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else -1

/-- Number of neighbours of `A` outside `Λ`. -/
def outDeg (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) (Λ : Finset 𝒯) (A : 𝒯) : ℕ :=
  {B : 𝒯 | B ∉ Λ ∧ tAdj 𝒯 A B}.ncard

/-- Energy in `Λ` with plus boundary condition. -/
def energyPlus (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) (Λ : Finset 𝒯) (σ : Λ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  -(1 / 2) * ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Λ × Λ)).filter (fun p : Λ × Λ => tAdj 𝒯 p.1.1 p.2.1),
      spinv (σ p.1) * spinv (σ p.2)
  - ∑ A : Λ, spinv (σ A) * (outDeg 𝒯 Λ A.1 : ℝ)

/-- `⟨σ_x⟩` in `Λ ∋ x` with plus boundary condition at inverse temperature `β`. -/
def magPlus (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) (β : ℝ) (Λ : Finset 𝒯) (x : 𝒯) (hx : x ∈ Λ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ σ : Λ → Bool, spinv (σ ⟨x, hx⟩) * Real.exp (-β * energyPlus 𝒯 Λ σ)) /
    ∑ σ : Λ → Bool, Real.exp (-β * energyPlus 𝒯 Λ σ)

/-- Infinite-volume plus-state magnetisation at `x` (monotone limit = infimum, by GKS). -/
def mPlus (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) (β : ℝ) (x : 𝒯) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ Λ : {Λ : Finset 𝒯 // x ∈ Λ}, magPlus 𝒯 β Λ.1 x Λ.2

/-! ### Discrete Dobrushin domains and interfaces -/

/-- A finite set of tiles with a boundary cycle `v`, `a = v 0`, `b = v j`. -/
structure DiscDomain (𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)) where
  D : Finset 𝒯
  L : ℕ
  v : Fin (L + 3) → ℂ
  j : ℕ

namespace DiscDomain
variable {𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)} (Dd : DiscDomain 𝒯)

/-- Cyclic indexing of the boundary cycle. -/
def vAt (k : ℕ) : ℂ := Dd.v ⟨k % (Dd.L + 3), Nat.mod_lt k (by omega)⟩

/-- `u w` is a boundary arc: between a tile of `D` and a tile outside `D`. -/
def BEdge (u w : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : 𝒯, A ∈ Dd.D ∧ ∃ B : 𝒯, B ∉ Dd.D ∧ ArcOf 𝒯 A.1 B.1 u w

/-- Well-formed discrete domain: `v` is a simple cycle listing exactly the boundary arcs. -/
def IsDisc : Prop :=
  Function.Injective Dd.v ∧ 0 < Dd.j ∧ Dd.j < Dd.L + 3 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < Dd.L + 3 → Dd.BEdge (Dd.vAt i) (Dd.vAt (i + 1))) ∧
  (∀ u w : ℂ, Dd.BEdge u w → ∃ i : ℕ, i < Dd.L + 3 ∧
      ((Dd.vAt i = u ∧ Dd.vAt (i + 1) = w) ∨ (Dd.vAt i = w ∧ Dd.vAt (i + 1) = u)))

/-- Dobrushin boundary value of the boundary arc `u w`: `+1` on the arc from `a` to `b`. -/
def bcVal (u w : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  if ∃ i : ℕ, i < Dd.j ∧ s(Dd.vAt i, Dd.vAt (i + 1)) = s(u, w) then 1 else -1

/-- Ising energy with Dobrushin boundary conditions. -/
def energy (σ : Dd.D → Bool) : ℝ :=
  -(1 / 2) * ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Dd.D × Dd.D)).filter
      (fun p : Dd.D × Dd.D => tAdj 𝒯 p.1.1 p.2.1), spinv (σ p.1) * spinv (σ p.2)
  - ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (Dd.L + 3), ∑ A : Dd.D,
      (if ∃ B : 𝒯, B ∉ Dd.D ∧ ArcOf 𝒯 A.1.1 B.1 (Dd.vAt i) (Dd.vAt (i + 1))
        then spinv (σ A) * (if i < Dd.j then 1 else -1) else 0)

/-- `u w` is an interface (disagreement) edge for `σ`. -/
def Disagree (σ : Dd.D → Bool) (u w : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : Dd.D, ∃ B : 𝒯, ArcOf 𝒯 A.1.1 B.1 u w ∧
    (if hB : B ∈ Dd.D then σ A ≠ σ ⟨B, hB⟩ else spinv (σ A) ≠ Dd.bcVal u w)

/-- `l` is an interface trail from `a` to `b`: consecutive vertices joined by disagreement edges,
no edge used twice. -/
def ValidTrail (σ : Dd.D → Bool) (l : List ℂ) : Prop :=
  2 ≤ l.length ∧ l.getD 0 0 = Dd.vAt 0 ∧ l.getD (l.length - 1) 0 = Dd.vAt Dd.j ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i + 1 < l.length → Dd.Disagree σ (l.getD i 0) (l.getD (i + 1) 0)) ∧
  (∀ i k : ℕ, i < k → k + 1 < l.length →
    s(l.getD i 0, l.getD (i + 1) 0) ≠ s(l.getD k 0, l.getD (k + 1) 0))

/-- Closed boundary polygon through `δ v_i`, 1-periodic in `s`. -/
def cyclePoly (δ : ℝ) (s : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  let x : ℝ := Int.fract s * ((Dd.L : ℝ) + 3)
  let k : ℕ := ⌊x⌋₊
  (δ : ℂ) * (Dd.vAt k + ((x - k : ℝ) : ℂ) * (Dd.vAt (k + 1) - Dd.vAt k))

end DiscDomain

/-- Polygonal curve on `[0,1]` through the points of `l` (at least two points). -/
def polyCurve (l : List ℂ) (t : unitInterval) : ℂ :=
  let m : ℕ := l.length - 1
  let s : ℝ := (t : ℝ) * (m : ℝ)
  let k : ℕ := min ⌊s⌋₊ (m - 1)
  l.getD k 0 + ((s - k : ℝ) : ℂ) * (l.getD (k + 1) 0 - l.getD k 0)

/-- Expectation of `F(δ · interface)` under the Dobrushin Ising measure at `β`. -/
def expect {𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)} (β : ℝ) (Dd : DiscDomain 𝒯) (δ : ℝ)
    (sel : (Dd.D → Bool) → List ℂ) (F : (unitInterval → ℂ) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ σ : Dd.D → Bool, Real.exp (-β * Dd.energy σ) *
      F (fun t : unitInterval => (δ : ℂ) * polyCurve (sel σ) t)) /
    ∑ σ : Dd.D → Bool, Real.exp (-β * Dd.energy σ)

/-! ### Curves, domains, SLE -/

/-- Distance between curves up to increasing reparametrisation. -/
def reparamDist (γ₁ γ₂ : unitInterval → ℂ) : ENNReal :=
  ⨅ (φ : unitInterval ≃ₜ unitInterval) (_ : Monotone φ), ⨆ t : unitInterval, edist (γ₁ t) (γ₂ (φ t))

/-- Test functions: bounded by 1 and 1-Lipschitz for `reparamDist`. -/
def TestFn (F : (unitInterval → ℂ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ γ : unitInterval → ℂ, |F γ| ≤ 1) ∧
  ∀ γ₁ γ₂ : unitInterval → ℂ, ENNReal.ofReal |F γ₁ - F γ₂| ≤ reparamDist γ₁ γ₂

/-- `f` maps the closed disc homeomorphically onto the closure of a Jordan domain, conformally on
the open disc. -/
def IsJordanMap (f : ℂ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn f (Metric.closedBall 0 1) ∧ Set.InjOn f (Metric.closedBall 0 1) ∧
  DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Metric.ball 0 1)

/-- `p` and `q` (1-periodic closed curves) are `ε`-close up to reparametrisation of the circle. -/
def FrechetClose (ε : ℝ) (p q : ℝ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous φ ∧
    ((StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, φ (s + 1) = φ s + 1) ∨
     (StrictAnti φ ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, φ (s + 1) = φ s - 1)) ∧
    ∀ s : ℝ, ‖p (φ s) - q s‖ ≤ ε

/-- The scaled discrete domains converge to `(f(𝔻), f(-1), f(1))`. -/
def DomConv {𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)} (f : ℂ → ℂ) (δ : ℕ → ℝ) (Dd : ℕ → DiscDomain 𝒯) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    FrechetClose ε ((Dd n).cyclePoly (δ n))
        (fun s : ℝ => f (Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * s : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))) ∧
    ‖(δ n : ℂ) * (Dd n).vAt 0 - f (-1)‖ ≤ ε ∧ ‖(δ n : ℂ) * (Dd n).vAt (Dd n).j - f 1‖ ≤ ε

/-- `W = √κ ·` standard Brownian motion. -/
def IsBM {Ω' : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ω'] (P : Measure Ω') (W : ℝ → Ω' → ℝ) (κ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ ω : Ω', W 0 ω = 0) ∧ (∀ ω : Ω', ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => W t ω) (Set.Ici 0)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, Measurable (W t)) ∧
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (τ : Fin (k + 1) → ℝ), τ 0 = 0 → StrictMono τ →
    P.map (fun ω : Ω' => fun i : Fin k => W (τ i.succ) ω - W (τ (Fin.castSucc i)) ω) =
      Measure.pi (fun i : Fin k =>
        ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 (Real.toNNReal (κ * (τ i.succ - τ (Fin.castSucc i)))))

/-- Upper half-plane. -/
def UHP : Set ℂ := {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}

/-- `ℍ \ η(0,t]`. -/
def slitDomain (η : ℝ → ℂ) (t : ℝ) : Set ℂ := UHP \ η '' Set.Ioc 0 t

/-- `η` is the simple chordal Loewner curve in `ℍ` from `0` with driving function `W`
(half-plane capacity parametrisation). -/
def DrivenBy (η : ℝ → ℂ) (W : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn η (Set.Ici 0) ∧ η 0 = 0 ∧ Set.InjOn η (Set.Ici 0) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → 0 < (η t).im) ∧
  ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ,
    DifferentiableOn ℂ g (slitDomain η t) ∧ Set.InjOn g (slitDomain η t) ∧
    g '' slitDomain η t = UHP ∧
    Tendsto (fun z : ℂ => z * (g z - z - 2 * (t : ℂ) / z))
      (Bornology.cobounded ℂ ⊓ 𝓟 (slitDomain η t)) (𝓝 0) ∧
    Tendsto g (𝓝[slitDomain η t] (η t)) (𝓝 (W t : ℂ))

/-- Möbius map `ℍ → 𝔻`, `0 ↦ -1`, `∞ ↦ 1`. -/
def mob (z : ℂ) : ℂ := (z - Complex.I) / (z + Complex.I)

/-- `Γ` is a reparametrisation to `[0,1]` of `f ∘ mob ∘ η` (ending at `f 1 = b`). -/
def IsSLECurve (f : ℂ → ℂ) (η : ℝ → ℂ) (Γ : unitInterval → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ θ : ℝ → ℝ, θ 0 = 0 ∧ ContinuousOn θ (Set.Ico 0 1) ∧ StrictMonoOn θ (Set.Ico 0 1) ∧
    Tendsto θ (𝓝[<] 1) atTop ∧
    (∀ s : unitInterval, (s : ℝ) < 1 → Γ s = f (mob (η (θ s)))) ∧ Γ 1 = f 1

/-- A probability space with `W = √3 B` and a Borel random curve `Γ` that is a.s. chordal SLE₃ in
`(f(𝔻), f(-1), f(1))`. -/
def IsSLE3Setup (f : ℂ → ℂ) {Ω' : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ω'] (P : Measure Ω')
    (W : ℝ → Ω' → ℝ) (Γ : Ω' → C(unitInterval, ℂ)) : Prop :=
  IsProbabilityMeasure P ∧ IsBM P W 3 ∧
  @Measurable Ω' C(unitInterval, ℂ) _ (borel C(unitInterval, ℂ)) Γ ∧
  ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, ∃ η : ℝ → ℂ, DrivenBy η (fun t : ℝ => W t ω) ∧
    Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => ‖η t‖) atTop atTop ∧ IsSLECurve f η (Γ ω)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ βc : ℝ, 0 < βc ∧ (∃ 𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ), IsHatTiling 𝒯) ∧
  (∀ 𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ), IsHatTiling 𝒯 → ∀ (x : 𝒯) (β : ℝ), 0 < β →
      (β ≤ βc → mPlus 𝒯 β x = 0) ∧ (βc < β → 0 < mPlus 𝒯 β x)) ∧
  ∀ 𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ), IsHatTiling 𝒯 → ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsJordanMap f →
    (∃ (Ω' : Type) (_ : MeasurableSpace Ω') (P : Measure Ω') (W : ℝ → Ω' → ℝ)
        (Γ : Ω' → C(unitInterval, ℂ)), IsSLE3Setup f P W Γ) ∧
    ∀ (Ω' : Type) [MeasurableSpace Ω'] (P : Measure Ω') (W : ℝ → Ω' → ℝ)
      (Γ : Ω' → C(unitInterval, ℂ)), IsSLE3Setup f P W Γ →
    ∀ (δ : ℕ → ℝ) (Dd : ℕ → DiscDomain 𝒯), (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < δ n) → Tendsto δ atTop (𝓝 0) →
      (∀ n : ℕ, (Dd n).IsDisc) → DomConv f δ Dd →
    ∀ sel : (n : ℕ) → ((Dd n).D → Bool) → List ℂ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (σ : (Dd n).D → Bool), (Dd n).ValidTrail σ (sel n σ)) →
    ∀ F : (unitInterval → ℂ) → ℝ, TestFn F →
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => expect βc (Dd n) (δ n) (sel n) F) atTop
        (𝓝 (∫ ω, F (Γ ω) ∂P))

end
